div.div: The object detector's added GPU wait follows the other processes' share of GPU time on a convex curve; the VLA sits on the compute co-tenant's curve, and a memory copy at the same GPU time adds nothing (illustrative numbers)
O = other processes' share of GPU-active time (percentage points)
C = the detector's added blocked time (ms per frame, above the no-load window)
dashed: predicted before the run, C at the high dose stays below R

no load
(O 0, C 0 ms)

compute, low dose
(O 40, C 40 ms)
[dose_curve_points, illustrative]

compute, middle dose
(O 60, C 80 ms)

compute, high dose
(O 80, C 160 ms)
slope 1 ms per point [dose_slopes, illustrative]
slope 2 ms per point [dose_slopes]
slope 4 ms per point [dose_slopes]

VLA arm = R (O 65, C 100 ms) [dose_vla_point, illustrative]
C* = curve at O 65 = 100 ms, so C*/R = 1 (my estimate from `dose_curve_points` and `dose_vla_point`)
memory-copy co-tenant, same GPU time as the low-dose arm: adds 0 ms [dram_null_added_ms, illustrative]

Correction kept visible. The first test's class "neither alone" (C about 40 % of R, my estimate from `dose_curve_points` and `dose_vla_point`) came from a compute arm at about 40 points against the VLA's 65: the low end of a convex curve. The first class stands as recorded.

Verdict as pre-registered: "dose explains". The VLA point lies on the compute co-tenant's curve (C*/R = 1, my estimate from `dose_curve_points` and `dose_vla_point`). Each extra point of O costs more than the last: slopes 1 / 2 / 4 ms per point [dose_slopes].

What adds nothing measurable at the VLA's dose
• DRAM traffic: the memory copy adds 0 ms [dram_null_added_ms].
• SM issue rate: the compute co-tenant issues far more often than the VLA, yet costs the same at the same share.
• Burst length: short vs long bursts at one share differ by 0 ms [burst_length_effect_ms, illustrative].

Two predictions were wrong (written before the run)
• high dose: predicted below R, measured 1.6 R (my estimate from `dose_curve_points` and `dose_vla_point`).
• burst length: predicted to matter, it did not. Bursts well below one time slice (under 1 ms) were not tested.

Why share, not traffic (page 05). "Work launched to the compute engine from work queues belonging to different CUDA contexts cannot execute concurrently." [mps_no_concurrency_quote] Without MPS the contexts take turns of about 1–5 ms [timeslice_ms, illustrative], so the detector waits for the others' turns plus each switch. The split between slice waiting and switch cost was not measured.
In the full stack, next to the VLA, most of the detector's rise is GPU wait (ms per frame added) [detector_vla_added_blocked_wait_run, illustrative]
blocked 70
CPU wait 20
run 10
sum 100 ms per frame, full stack -> full stack + VLA (a different row from the dose curve; my estimate from `detector_vla_added_blocked_wait_run`)

Caveats. Measured in a reduced row (the depth camera service and the detector only), idle CPU pool, one window per arm. In the full stack the mechanism is expected, not tested; full-stack windows sit below the curve in a post-hoc reading, because the detector also waits for the CPU there and meets less GPU contention per frame (not separated from other causes). The victim metric is blocked time: neither running nor waiting for a CPU, mostly waiting for the GPU. O removes the detector's own GPU time; added GPU busy would include it and understate the dose. Straight segments join the points; the curve between them is not measured. All measured values are an illustrative measurement.

Legend
green line + filled circles = compute co-tenant arms; hollow circle = no-load window
black square = the VLA arm (R)
hollow dashed orange square = memory-copy co-tenant
dashed black line = prediction written before the run
purple dashed box = a correction
green box = the pre-registered verdict
stacked bar: solid = illustrative measured share; dashed = slower run

Sources. Note B1. Contexts and time-slicing: ../../nvidia-gpu-anatomy/ (note 07). C* and the ratios to R are straight-line arithmetic on the points.
Illustrative (round teaching numbers that keep the shape of a finding; not measurements): dose_curve_points, dose_slopes, dose_vla_point, dram_null_added_ms, burst_length_effect_ms, timeslice_ms, detector_vla_added_blocked_wait_run.
Public: mps_no_concurrency_quote = https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/mps/architecture.html.
